claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis (c. 310/320–403); bishop of Salamis from 367; friend of Jerome.
The Anchor of Faith written 374; Trinitarian exposition against Arianism.
SCOPE: Chapter II (Spirit to seekers; Peter's confession; Trinity in unity).
Epiphanius was born at Besanduk, near Eleutheropolis, in Judea, after 310 and died in 403.
Epiphanius was the Bishop of Constantia (Salamis), the metropolis of the Island of Cyprus.
Epiphanius was nominated as bishop in 367 and served for nearly forty years.
Epiphanius founded a monastery at Besanduk and was ordained to the priesthood before becoming bishop.
While very young, Epiphanius followed the monastic life in Egypt.
The Ancoratus, or 'The Well-Anchored,' was written in 374 at the instance of his correspondents.
